title: Steady Fraction Calibration & Pin Playbook
content:
Quick goal: produce a small, repeatable playbook for: (a) pinning model versions for a slow-ramp canary, (b) calibrating traffic fractions by client cohort, and (c) a lightweight telemetry surface + hard triggers for rollback.

Context / why this doc exists:
- We often need a middle-ground between full canary and immediate full-roll. Several teams want deterministic pinning + gradual traffic increase but with client-weighted fractions (eg mobile vs web).
- Past incidents: traffic jump after mis-pin (INF-3490) and delayed detection because thresholds were too loose. Need clearer fractions and concrete preflight checks.

High level approach (sketch):
1) Preflight (local + staging) — verify model artifact, init KV warmup, basic perf smoke.
  - smoke queries: 6 short prompts + 2 long prompts (>=1024 tokens) to validate no OOMs and consistent latency
  - check: stable log-prob distribution compared to baseline (quick diff, not deep eval)
  - SRE: confirm node health and GPU memory headroom > 15% across pool
  - artifacts: include PR link and pinned model digest SHA in rollout ticket

2) Pin strategy (what to pin where):
  - step 0: create rollout ticket with pinned version string, canary cohort list, and metric owners
  - for Hosted API: use route-level pinning (config key: route.model_pin = <sha>)
  - for Dedicated: apply node pool label + immutable deployment artifact (documented in ticket)
  - record fallback model id (compatible fallback) in ticket metadata

3) Traffic fraction calibration (core of this doc) — goal: 0 -> target in safe increments over N windows
  - default fraction steps: [0.005, 0.02, 0.05, 0.12, 0.25, 0.5] (fractions of total client traffic)
  - window durations (min): 15m, 30m, 45m, 1h, 2h, 4h (can compress if metrics stable)
  - client-weighting: allocate fractions to cohorts, not uniformly. Example: {mobile: 0.6, web: 0.3, api-partners: 0.1}
  - practical: when adding a step, ensure cohort-level absolute qps for that cohort >= 5 qps or else extend window

4) Acceptance checks per window (fast pass/fail):
  - latency (p95) <= baseline_p95 * 1.25 AND absolute p95 < 600ms for hosted tier (adjust per region/tier)
  - error rate (5xx) delta <= +0.2 percentage points (if baseline 0.1%, allow up to 0.3%)
  - quality guardrails: small fixed prompt set (10 prompts) auto-eval: pass if mean ROUGE/EM-like proxy delta < 3% (quick lexical check), AND no high-severity hallucination examples (manual review if flagged)
  - resource signals: GPU utilization change relative to baseline < +20% and mem headroom not decreasing below 10%
  - billing spike: tokens per minute increase > +50% -> hold and investigate

5) Hard rollback triggers (immediate rollback):
  - sustained p95 > baseline * 1.5 for > 5m
  - error rate delta > +1.0 percentage point for > 3m
  - OOM/eviction events or node restarts in canary pool
  - model producing classification/regression drift on sentinel prompts (high-confidence mismatch)

6) Soft stop / pause conditions (human review):
  - slow quality degradation (quality metric delta between steps 1-3 but not above hard threshold)
  - client-level complaints/ticket opened referencing regressions
  - telemetry gaps (missing traces/logs)

7) Roll-forward rules (post-checks):
  - if window passes all acceptance checks, move to next fraction step and annotate ticket with timestamps and metric snapshots
  - if a window fails a soft stop, reduce fraction to previous step and open an investigation; do not expand for at least 2h after mitigation
  - track cumulative exposure: never exceed X user-minutes without signoff for large model changes (X TBD per release class)

8) Telemetry minimal surface (what I want visible on slim dashboard):
  - p50/p95/p99 latency by cohort; error rate by cohort; tokens/min; qps; GPU utilization; mem headroom
  - quick diff overlay (current vs baseline) for each metric
  - sample output sink: surface 10 random responses (redact PII) for manual QA
  - canary-specific logs: node restarts, eviction events, OOMs, container kill reasons

9) Pre-commit checklist (before first fraction):
  - [ ] rollout ticket created with model digest and fallback model
  - [ ] rollout plan documented + cohort fraction mapping
  - [ ] SRE thumbs-up on capacity + warmup plan
  - [ ] QA quick pass results attached (smoke prompts + sample outputs)
  - [ ] Observability links added to ticket (dashboards, trace links)
  - [ ] Authorize list of on-call responders and escalation path

10) Example small-run script (manual ops steps, shorthand):
  - create pin: curl -X POST /admin/pins -d '{"route":"/chat","model":"model@sha:abc123"}' 
  - set traffic fraction: PATCH /admin/traffic-splits route=/chat body={"cohorts": {"mobile":0.005}}
  - verify: check dashboard, run smoke queries locally, wait window
  - notes: automation exists in infra repo (scripts/rollout-deploy.sh) — prefer script when non-exploratory

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Decide final cumulative exposure cap (user-minutes) for major vs minor model bumps. See INF-3421 for proposal.
- Build mini automation to compute "cohort absolute qps" from historical traffic to warn when step fractions yield < 5 qps
- Possible addition: dynamic windowing (reduce step duration if variance < threshold) — need SRE buy-in

Runbook snippets (for on-call):
- If immediate rollback required: set route.pin to fallback model SHA, set fraction to 0 for all cohorts, notify #releases and escalate to 2nd on-call.
- If telemetry missing: pause rollout, try flush-forward (restart obs agent on canary nodes), then continue only once metrics restored.

Random personal notes (scratch):
- Keep steps conservative for now — a lot of flaky infra in APAC clusters.
- Might try an "anchor cohort" approach: select a small set of internal clients (prod-sim) that always get first exposure for big changes. Good for early QA but has privacy/workflow downsides.
- Need to align with product for partner API contracts (they may require opt-in or advance notice).

End state: short, repeatable checklist + small automation to set fractions and capture metric snapshots. Then move the playbook to Confluence as the canonical release playbook and link from infra scripts.

Notes-to-self: clean this up after next canary (planned 2025-02-06) and fold in any corrections from Priya/Liam.
